subject.title: Feature: Message continuation marker for batched input (cost savings)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit, configurable continuation-marker contract, or keep timer/adaptive inbound aggregation as the supported way to combine rapid user messages?
rationale: Either direction establishes user-visible delivery timing and configuration semantics across channels; source evidence shows the requested marker behavior is not an existing bug fix.

options.title: Adopt explicit continuation markers
options.body: Sponsor a shared inbound feature with defined marker, timeout, command/media, ordering, and typing semantics across supported channels.

options.title: Prefer time-based aggregation
options.body: Keep the existing debounce/queue model as the supported solution and close this request only after documenting that product choice.

options.title: Defer the aggregation contract
options.body: Leave this issue open without implementation until channel and session-state ownership can define the common behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt explicit continuation markers
recommendation.body: Sponsor a shared inbound feature with defined marker, timeout, command/media, ordering, and typing semantics across supported channels.

likelyOwner.reason: The existing review and shared inbound-debounce history make this the strongest available routing candidate.
